# A context read written inside a slot population belongs to the caller, so the
# context lowering has to see it there. It did not: the reachability scan, the
# call-edge scan and the provider threading each walked a NodeInst's children
# and skipped its Slots, so the enclosing component was never marked as reading
# the context, no hidden parameter was threaded to it, and the *ir.ContextRead
# survived lowering to reach codegen -- where irwalk.EvalExpr has no case for
# one and every platform panicked.
#
# Each assertion below is the context's value arriving at the slot body on one
# target. A panic is the regression this catches on all three.

sngl generate --platform=html --lang=none --out=html read.sngl
grep 'var __ctx_theme = "light"' html/index.html
grep 'textContent = __ctx_theme' html/index.html

sngl generate --platform=android --lang=kotlin --out=android read.sngl
grep 'light' android/MainScreen.kt

sngl generate --platform=bubbletea --lang=go --out=bt read.sngl
grep 'light' bt/model.go

# A provider wrapping the call site. The read is lexically the caller's, so it
# resolves against the provider the caller sits under and not the context's
# default -- threading that walked Children alone would put "light" here, which
# is a wrong answer rather than a crash.
sngl generate --platform=html --lang=none --out=prov provided.sngl
grep '<span>dark</span>' prov/index.html
! grep 'light' prov/index.html

-- read.sngl --
import . "sngl:ui"

context #theme("light")

component framed(slot caption) {
    caption {
        text(value="(none)")
    }
}

component main {
    framed() {
        slot caption {
            text(value=theme)
        }
    }
}

-- provided.sngl --
import . "sngl:ui"

context #theme("light")

component framed(slot caption) {
    caption {
        text(value="(none)")
    }
}

component main {
    theme("dark") {
        framed() {
            slot caption {
                text(value=theme)
            }
        }
    }
}
